answer: Treat identities as an orchard audited by a ridge-distance rule. Quarterly a sampler draws 5% of identities and measures the embedding distance between past answers and the median consensus. Scores must stay on a ridge between 0.15 and 0.45: below 0.15 an answer mirrors the crowd, the mark of template farms; above 0.45 it is noise. Violations burn 5% of deposit; one appeal per epoch. An attacker running N clones must keep each clone's reasoning in that band, so content cost grows linearly with no reuse, while its own mass shifts the median, pushing clones off the ridge.
